frames.slice_level: Upper thorax, at or just above the aortic arch (approximately T2-T4). Trachea round and midline; no arch contour resolved.
Carina / proximal main bronchi, approximately T5-T6. Airway seen centrally as a transverse lucency at the bifurcation.
Below the carina, at the main bronchi / bronchus intermedius, approximately T6-T7. Both bronchi visible as paired lucencies within the mediastinum.
Lower thorax at heart level, approximately T7-T8. Heart occupies most of the mediastinum; bronchus intermedius and left lower lobe bronchus visible as paired lucencies.
Lower thorax approaching the lung bases, approximately T8-T9. Heart occupies the central mediastinum; both lower lobes broadly in view.
Lung bases approaching the diaphragm, approximately T9-T10. Lung cross-sections reducing; central soft tissue is heart with diaphragm and upper abdominal contents beginning to enter the field.

cases.impression: Six contiguous axial levels of an unenhanced chest CT on soft-tissue window, descending from the upper thorax to the lung bases. The upper three levels are unremarkable. The lower three demonstrate a bilateral basal parenchymal process, right greater than left, with posterior and dependent predominance. On the right there is extensive heterogeneous opacity containing multiple small rounded and tubular air-density lucencies on a background of coarse reticular and branching lines. On the left, evident on the most caudal frame, there are clustered small nodular and short branching opacities of similar character but lesser extent, with the anterior left lung well aerated. The left-sided involvement was not apparent one level cranial, so the process is either more caudal on the left or was under-called there; these frames cannot distinguish those. The abnormality is definitely present and is not vascular — vessels do not contain air-density lucencies. Its nature is not settled here: bronchiectasis with mucus plugging, aspiration or bronchopneumonia, and chronic infection with bronchiolitis are all live considerations, with fibrotic change less likely given the asymmetry. No pneumothorax and no large pleural collection at the levels imaged; airway patent and midline throughout; bones intact. This is a significant bilateral finding that warrants review of the actual study on a lung window, with clinical context, rather than any conclusion drawn from screenshots.

findings.location: right lower lobe, extending from the perihilar region laterally and posteriorly
left lower lobe, posterior and dependent
